text:
Kent Johnson ended it 2:22 into overtime, a snap shot that finished a night in which Columbus built a three-goal lead in the first period, watched Philadelphia erase it, and still walked out with the win. Johnson, drafted fifth overall by the Blue Jackets in 2021 out of Michigan, scored twice and added an assist. Adam Fantilli and Denton Mateychuk scored the other first-period goals.

The result flatters Columbus. By expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of goals, PHI led 4.02 to 2.11 and attempted 66 shots to 37. Our simulation of every shot says the Flyers deserved to win 80 percent of the time. The Blue Jackets were the better team for one period, then spent the rest of the night defending. The third was lopsided: PHI out-chanced CBJ 1.48 to 0.15, and Trevor Zegras and Jamie Drysdale scored on either side of the final five minutes, Drysdale's deflection tying it with 11 seconds left in regulation.

Cam Talbot is the reason it held. He stopped 28 of 31 shots and saved about one goal more than the chances against him should have allowed, which is the margin between Columbus winning and losing. Dan Vladar went the other way for PHI, allowing nearly two goals more than his 15 shots against deserved, and that early hole is what the Flyers spent the night climbing out of. The data gives us no streaks or standings for either side, so we'll leave it at this: Philadelphia played well enough to take the points and got one for the effort, while Columbus took two on the strength of a hot first period and its goalie.
